newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt languishes at lower levels,losses seen.
newsitem.headline: German debt languishes at lower levels,losses seen.

text.p: German debt traded mostly sideways at lower levels on Thursday as stronger than expected economic data and bearish comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer helped brake the recent rally.
"Clearly the recent days' euphoria is gone," said a dealer, adding that today's consolidation would likely continue on Friday and into the next week.
By 1549 GMT the March Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB, was down four basis points at 103.46, having traded between 103.46 and 103.12 today.
Meanwhile the benchmark cash bond was trading at 103.52, yielding 5.52 percent, after trading at 103.58 on Wednesday.

After the German bond market had been riding high on ongoing negative economic news, the rally appeared broken today as both January business confidence showed stronger results and money supply had grown more strongly than expected.

The Bundesbank reported M3 money supply, one of its key policy indicators, grew at an 11.7 percent rate as compared with the fourth quarter 1996 average rate. This exceeds the bank's self-set 3.5 to 6.5 percent growth corridor and appeared to reduce the chances for another rate cut.

But more important, dealers said comments from Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer that a decline in Germany's interest rates would be unlikely in the short-term poured cold water on hopes for another easing.
The Bundesbank kept its three leading interest rates unchanged at its policy-setting council meeting today, meeting market expectations.
"Under these conditions the market could fall back past the 103 level and arrive comfortably at 102.75," another dealer said.
On the other hand some dealers remain optimistic on gains.
"This market is very resilient and since there is no chance that the Bundesbank will raise interest rates, the market will remain quite well supported," added another dealer.
But most agree that the consolidation will last at least into the weekend.
